body.statement: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying the displayed rank conditions, profiling the \(J\)-coordinate map \(q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x)\) over the unrestricted path of \(\delta_1^0(x)\) yields the observed normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\) for \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\), of rank \(J-1\). For either branch, \(\mathcal T_b(P_0)=\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{b,x}s]=0\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\) and \(\mathcal I_b(P_0)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}\). Consequently, \(\phi_b=\sum_x g_{b,x}-R_b^{\prime}\{E_{P_{0,O}}[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}E_{P_{0,O}}[R_b\sum_xg_{b,x}]\), with redundant PT and SC rows handled by the Moore--Penrose inverse.
body.justification: This gives the two branch faces in one observed-data Hilbert space and exposes the SC-weight derivative normals that a PT-only calculation omits.
body.gap: ChenSantAnnaXie2025, Theorem 3.1, derives the PT canonical gradient; SunXieZhang2025, Appendix equations (A.5) and (A.13), gives estimator-specific branch influence laws, but neither paper characterizes both affine influence classes at their intersection.
body.consumer: The normal-form representation is the input required to calculate an identification-robust standard error for the Alaska minimum-wage analysis in SunXieZhang2025.
